pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints CE Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Social Media
Welcome to All Saints CE Primary School
I have great pleasure in welcoming you to the All Saints C.E. Primary School website. We are a one form entry Church of England Primary School in Sidley, on the outskirts of Bexhill, East Sussex. We are an inclusive school that values each of our pupils as individuals. We take great pride in our community and in our desire for each child to reach their potential. We hope this website gives you a flavour of what life is like here and why we are a popular choice for parents. Mr Mike Taylor, Headteacher
Below is a video narrated by two of our prefects, explaining what they love about our school.

Friendship

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints CE Primary School - Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
‘The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.’ Ludwig Wittgenstein
Why is language learning important for children?
When children learn a new language, they are introduced to customs and values belonging to a different society. This encourages them to think from a new point of view.
Learning a new language reinforces understanding of English, develops confidence and encourages children to solve problems and ask questions.
The Intent of the teaching of Spanish at All Saints is to inspire curiosity and a love of languages that children will strengthen as they develop and progress through Key Stage 2.
As well as encouraging children to enjoy the experience of learning to communicate in another language, our MFL curriculum also inspires them to develop curiosity and respect for other cultures and lifestyles.
They will be taught appropriate balance of spoken and written language. This will lay the foundations for further foreign language teaching at Key Stage 3. Children will be taught to understand and communicate ideas, facts and feelings in speech and writing, focused on familiar and routine matters, using their knowledge of phonology, grammatical structures and vocabulary.

After School clubs and Breakfast Club
You can book your sessions through the Arbor App Club section
Children are offered a fruit and biscuit snack - they are encouraged to eat the fruit snack followed by either a simple savoury or sweet biscuit (including rice cakes, cheddars or rich tea biscuits as some of the wide range of choices). Children are also able to bring their own snack should the choose, as long as it contains no nuts.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints CE Primary School - Our Theologically Rooted Vision
pageCache.text:
Our Theologically Rooted Vision
Koinonia is the Christian value that is rooted in our theological foundations; we believe “If we walk in the light as he walked in the light we have fellowship (koinonia) with one another” (1 John 1:7). We nurture responsible, resilient and reflective members of our society and, by reflecting through worship upon our position as part of God’s creation, we encourage all to follow Christ’s example.
Our shared ideals of Common Grace and Fellowship promote a culture of aspiration, respect and encouragement in order that everyone reaches their full potential.
Through our relationship with the church, local community and environment, we enrich the learning opportunities we offer. Central to our vision for our children is our holistic curriculum which, with high expectations, encourages academic accomplishment and opportunities to flourish within a Christian ethos.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints CE Primary School - Sports Premium
pageCache.text:
Sports Premium
At All Saints CE Primary School, we recognise the contribution of PE to the health and well-being of the children. We believe that a varied PE curriculum and extra-curricular activities and opportunities have a positive influence on the concentration, self-esteem, attitude to learning and achievement of all our children. We believe that Physical education and sport contribute to the holistic development of children; through participation in sport and physical education, the children learn more about key values such as teamwork, fair play and respect for themselves and others. There is significant evidence to show the positive effects of sport and exercise on children’s health, growth and development. Sport also provides a healthy environment for young people to learn how to deal with competition and how to cope with both winning and losing. What is the Sports’ Premium?
Schools receive PE and sport premium funding based on the number of pupils in years 1 to 6. Schools with 17 or more eligible pupils receive £16,000 and an additional payment of £10 per pupil. Below is how we propose to use this funding to address the key indicators at our school.

School Dinners
/docs/All_Saints_Welcome_Letter.docx
How to order a meal through Relish, please see the link below.
Cut-off to order is midnight so if you want a dinner on Wednesday this has to be ordered by midnight on Tuesday.
Meals are £3 each for children in nursery or from Year 3 to Year 6 unless you receive Free School Meals due to benefits you may receive.
If you are not sure if you are entitled to Free School Meals, please contact the school office and you will be provided with an application form and we can check with the FSM team at East Sussex County Council.
If you are entitled to FSM then you will also receive the HUGGG vouchers from the local authority at holiday times.
If your child is in Reception Class, Year 1 or Year 2 they receive the Universal free meal from the government so there is no charge.
All nursery meals are payable regardless of your circumstances.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints CE Primary School - Curriculum Implementation
pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum Implementation
As a primary school, our core purpose is to ensure that all our pupils reach their potential in all areas of the curriculum, leaving this school with both high levels of attainment and having progressed well from their starting point. We believe that we will be more successful if this core goal is enshrined in a clear and shared approach to teaching and learning and to the school ethos and this is done through our Teaching and learning Policy. We use evidence based research to ensure our approaches will be effective. Teachers regularly reflect upon how they teach to ensure we continually strive to improve.
Teaching and Learning Policy
Our curriculum is designed and delivered to ensure children can transfer key information to long-term memory. All knowledge and skills are sequenced so learning builds as pupils move through nursery and school. Each subject is led by a teacher and the progression of knowledge produced for each subject enables learning and the acquisition of knowledge to be coherently sequenced; teachers know what has been learned before in each subject area and there are clearly defined end-points.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints CE Primary School - SEN Information
pageCache.text:
SEN Information
Special Educational Needs Information Report 2025-26
The Children and Families Act 2014 says that all maintained schools must
publish a Special Educational Needs (SEN) Information Report every year.
This report explains how our school meets the needs of children with SEN. It
will be shown on our school website and in the ‘local offer’ at this link.
In the report, we explain how we meet our duties towards pupils with special
educational needs and disabilities. This report is also our SEN policy. This
report is also the information we provide to the East Sussex local offer which
show the support that is available for children and young people with special
educational needs and disabilities in East Sussex.
We will review this report every year and will involve pupils and parents. If
you want to give us your views about the report, please contact the school
If you are thinking of applying for a place, contact Julie Stilwell, our school
secretary. If your child is already at the school, you should talk to the child’s class
teacher. School phone number 01424 219083.
The Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCO) is responsible for
managing and co-ordinating the support for children with special educational
needs, including those who have Education Health and Care (EHC) plans.
Please click on link below for the full report.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints CE Primary School - Breakfast Club
pageCache.text:
All Saints C E Primary School has a Breakfast Club for our children at this school and children who attend our nursery.
It is available Monday to Friday starting at 7.50am until 8.30am in our School Hall. Children arrive at front of school from 7.50am. Breakfast includes cereal, toast, milk and water.
From September 2025 until end of July 2026 the daily charge will be £2.65 for school children and £3.60 for nursery children.
From September 2026 the daily charge will be £2.70 for school children and £3.73 for nursery children.
If your child wishes to attend Breakfast Club, please book through the Arbor App
